qs.q:
Gap year — Which person…

A=Annabelle (gap year = escape from responsibility, privilege of the wealthy, parents hard to persuade, mostly followed news from home, didn't meet real world or self)
B=Bradley (economic difficulties but funded programmes exist, volunteering/work experience helps job applications, helps local economies)
C=Cheryl (rising uni fees will reduce gap years — which is good, work experience = photocopier/coffee trays, friends dived in but she spent year looking for excuse to return)
D=Dominic (camping/preservation project, gap year makes academic deadlines seem manageable, investment must be worthwhile, predeparture education essential)
E=Elaine (overseas volunteer work is hard, question of impact — projects now benefit traveller not community)
F=Forrest (exotic destination, British pound goes far, absence of internet = rewarding cut-off, gap year made him who he is today, no plans = freedom)

0. says that the exchange rate of the British currency is favourable for a gap year? [F=Forrest]
1. sarcastically refers to job preparation schemes in gap year programmes?
2. says they did not make any serious plans for activities during their gap year?
3. says that a gap year can be mistaken for a vacation?
4. mentions the benefits of a gap year experience for later academic work?
5. says a gap year is an excuse for avoiding making life decisions?
6. claims an administrative educational decision might prevent students from taking a gap year?
7. says that gap year trends reinforce social inequality?
8. claims that gap year students have better career opportunities?
9. questions if gap year students bring any advantages to the places they stay in?
10. says planning is crucial for a beneficial gap year?
11. sees benefits in being uninformed about world affairs?
12. says that they did their gap year unwillingly?
items: 1 — sarcastically refers to job preparation schemes?
2 — says they did not make any serious plans for activities?
3 — says a gap year can be mistaken for a vacation?
4 — mentions benefits of gap year for later academic work?
5 — says a gap year is an excuse for avoiding life decisions?
6 — claims an educational decision might prevent students from taking a gap year?
7 — says gap year trends reinforce social inequality?
8 — claims gap year students have better career opportunities?
9 — questions if gap year students bring advantages to places they stay?
10 — says planning is crucial for a beneficial gap year?
11 — sees benefits in being uninformed about world affairs?
12 — says they did their gap year unwillingly?

qs.q:
Going up?

"It is the NOVEL CONCEPT OF VERTICAL LAYERED STRUCTURES that will REVOLUTIONIZE the contours of future cities."

What will impact modern urban planning most?
A Rapid population growth.
B Environmental changes.
C Potential catastrophes.
D Innovative constructions.

Going up?

"These modern skyscrapers will not only PRODUCE ENERGY AND FOOD, but will also provide their occupants with CLEAN WATER."

What will urban ecosystems be like?
A Spacious.
B Productive.
C Landlocked.
D Expensive.

Going up?

"Our buildings will have a so-called nervous system... create comfortable homes. The skyscraper will USE THE SURROUNDINGS TO CREATE SUSTAINABLE LIVING."

According to paragraph 3, what will architects do?
A They will cross construction limits in architecture.
B They will irritate tenants in the surrounding houses.
C They will use a building's environment to its maximum.
D They will only build in areas with dense green forests.
opts: They will cross construction limits in architecture.
They will irritate tenants in the surrounding houses.
They will use a building's environment to its maximum.
They will only build in areas with dense green forests.

qs.q:
Going up?

"Building facades will use cement to absorb CO₂, paint to HARNESS SOLAR ENERGY, bio fuel from algae, and wind turbines to manufacture DRINKING WATER."

What will not be produced by skyscrapers?
A Electricity.
B Bio fuel.
C Water.
D Clean air.

Going up?

"We are going to use SUPER-COMPRESSED MASS TIMBER PANELS in giant blocks."

B Concrete.
C Wood.
D Brick.

Going up?

"The bottom line here is NOT TO CHANGE THE ENGINEERING, but the CONCEPTS IN OUR HEADS. AND THAT IS THE MOST DEMANDING TASK OF ALL."

What is the main idea expressed in the last paragraph?
A Altering our thinking is a challenge.
B Fictional images are our future.
C The need for change is exaggerated.
D Current science is to be changed.
opts: Altering our thinking is a challenge.
The need for change is exaggerated.
Current science is to be changed.

qs.q:
Lake Malawi's lost resort

"We tried a couple of lodges, but they were closed, or had no vacancies, or just didn't like the look of us. (19) ____. We were beginning to get worried."

A The three of them and the boyfriend all got behind the car and started to shove.
B We were directed to other, more remote places, which either didn't exist, or were also full.
C No one knew whether they would ever come again.
D They were definitely not well-trodden – they were hardly more than faint trails.
E We were woken by bright sunlight through the cracks in the bamboo wall, and the sound of their voices.
F Getting out to assess the situation, we saw it was even worse than we had imagined.
G As they drew closer, two boys appeared, followed by an older man.
H I felt alternating waves of fear and comfort, for I realised that if they wanted to rob us, they could have done so already.
opts: A — They all got behind the car and started to shove.
B — We were directed to other, more remote places, which either didn't exist, or were also full.
C — No one knew whether they would ever come again.
D — They were hardly more than faint trails.
E — We were woken by bright sunlight through the bamboo wall.
F — Getting out to assess the situation, we saw it was even worse.
G — As they drew closer, two boys appeared, followed by an older man.
H — I felt waves of fear and comfort.
